verdict.rationale: Sill pairs each device with the Mac once, after which only paired devices can connect. Combined with Launch at Login, this lets paired devices reach the Mac without someone re-pairing at the host each time. The initial pairing still needs the on-screen code to be read at the Mac or through screen sharing, and the docs never say that later connections need no confirmation on the host. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that connections need no host-side acceptance, admin pre-provisioning of credentials without a code exchange at the host, access at the login window or locked screen, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can set up unattended access to a machine with credentials configured in advance, so no one has to sit at the host to accept

citations.quote: Each iPhone or iPad pairs with your Mac once. After that, only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
To have Sill open by itself then, choose Launch at Login in the Sill menu, or turn it on in Sill’s Settings › General.
Turn on Show the pairing window to screen sharing in Sill’s Settings › Devices on your Mac; while it’s on, anyone who can see your Mac’s screen remotely can read the code.
Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
